title: The Christmas Eve Rescue That Did Not Save Lilium's Electric Jet
conflicts: Money raised: about €1.5 billion (dpa via Tagesspiegel/Stuttgarter Zeitung, aeroTELEGRAPH) vs more than $1 billion (TechCrunch) vs $1.1 billion since 2021 (Skift); story uses dpa's figure, attributed. Orders: 780 (company claim via AVweb/FLYING) vs about 700 firm and pre-orders (dpa); story says 'hundreds'. Jobs: dpa corrected 1,000 to 750 rehired; aero.international says about 1,000; GÖRG says around 775 saved; story uses about 750. Rescue sum €200m (dpa, AOPA) vs €210m (FLYING); story says about €200m. Investor names differ between dpa and the administrators' lawyers; story names only the consortium and assigns no blame.
notes: Wiegand had stepped down as CEO on 1 August 2022 (Klaus Roewe took over) and was chief engineer and board member during the insolvencies; the story says so plainly and uses Wiegand's own June 2023 New Atlas interview and his October 2024 warning (paraphrased, since only an English translation of his Bild remark is available). Quote stance complicates: Confucius distinguishes running out of strength midway from limiting oneself, and the connection leaves open whether the plan asked too much.
